questions.title: Opportunistic parasites: self-limited in healthy hosts, severe in immunocompromised
questions.question: Opportunistic parasites?

options.A: Cause a self-limited infestation in healthy individuals but cause severe diseases to immunocompromised patients
options.B: Live in the body of its host in another place than its normal one
options.C: Are artifacts which could be mistaken as parasite during examination,like some pollen grains or yeasts
options.D: Establish themselves in a host which is not its ordinary one

explanations.A: Correct. Opportunistic parasites typically cause only a mild, self-limited infestation in an immunocompetent host, but can cause severe, even life-threatening disease once the host becomes immunocompromised. This immune-status-dependent severity is the defining feature of an opportunistic parasite, distinguishing it from parasites that cause similar disease regardless of host immune status.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Living in an abnormal body site within the normal host describes an erratic parasite, not an opportunistic one.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Being an artifact mistaken for a parasite (such as a pollen grain or free-living yeast) describes a pseudoparasite, not a true opportunistic parasite.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Establishing itself in a host species other than its ordinary one describes an incidental (accidental) parasite, not an opportunistic one.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Since option A correctly captures the defining, immune-status-dependent feature of an opportunistic parasite, "none of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: State that opportunistic parasites cause self-limited disease in immunocompetent hosts but severe disease in immunocompromised hosts.
